title: Send the blame back through attention, and build a copy decoder
brief: Write the backward rule for the softmax, the blend, and the whole additive attention, checked against finite differences. Then stack the weights into an alignment matrix and hand-set a scorer so each step reads the right source position.
hints: softmax_backward: dscores = weights * (dweights - np.sum(weights * dweights)). The subtracted number is the weighted average of dweights, and the answer always sums to zero.
context_backward: context = weights @ values, so dweights = values @ dcontext and dvalues = np.outer(weights, dcontext).
In attention_backward, rerun the forward pass first. Keep t = np.tanh(u), because the tanh step needs 1 - t**2.
The query is added to every row of u, so sum du over axis 0 before using it for dW1 and dquery: dW1 = np.outer(du.sum(axis=0), query). Then dW2 = du.T @ keys, dkeys = du @ W2, and dv = t.T @ dscores.

alignment_matrix calls additive_attention once per query and stacks the results: contexts with np.stack, weights as the rows of A. mean_summary is the mean of the one-hot rows of np.eye(vocab_size)[source_tokens].

For decode_with_attention, use queries = keys = 10 * np.eye(T), values = one-hot rows for the source tokens, W1 = W2 = np.eye(T), and v = v_sign * 10 * np.ones(T). Read the decoded token as int(np.argmax(context)) for each row of contexts.
